Style: stylized 3D animated feature film, expressive faces, 9:16.
Setting: Thanksgiving dining room under a warm but harsh overhead chandelier; a crowded table with steam rising off the turkey, relatives packed shoulder to shoulder in the background who laugh on cue; Aiden sits at the far end in a cooler pool of shadow.
Shots (hard cuts):
1. 0.0–1.2 s. Wide eye-level shot down the length of the table, quick drift in. Mom reaches for the potato bowl while Rick, across the packed table, already levels his fork at Aiden. Mom says, brightly: "Pass the potatoes, please."
2. 1.2–3.8 s. Medium close-up on Rick, quick push-in. Rick jabs his fork across the table, his grin stretching smug and wide. Uncle Rick booms: "So Aiden, still doing your little internet trading?"
3. 3.8–5.0 s. Medium close-up on Aiden, static. Aiden calmly sets his fork down, face even. Aiden says: "It's going well, actually."
4. 5.0–7.2 s. Low-angle close-up on Rick, fast push-in. Rick leans back and spreads his arms wide to the table, playing to the crowd. Uncle Rick scoffs loudly: "Going well? You live in your mom's basement."
5. 7.2–8.2 s. Wide shot of the table, slight handheld shake. The whole table bursts out laughing; relatives throw their heads back and slap the table, Rick loudest of all, Mom caught mid-wince.
6. 8.2–9.4 s. Close-up on Aiden, shallow focus, laughing relatives blurred around him. He is the only one not laughing; his face burns red, knuckles white around the fork, held for a beat.
7. 9.4–10.5 s. Medium close-up on Mom, static. She shoots Rick a sharp look, brows pulled down. Mom snaps: "Rick, leave him alone."
8. 10.5–11.5 s. Tight close-up on Aiden's eyes, slow push-in. The laughter dies away; his eyes lock on Rick, unblinking.
9. 11.5–13.2 s. Extreme close-up on Aiden, static, hold. He never breaks eye contact. Aiden says quietly: "Give me a year." Hold half a second on his stare as Rick's smirk flickers in the soft background.
10. 13.2–15.0 s. Wide shot from Rick's end of the table, static. Aiden shoves his chair back, throws his napkin onto his plate and storms out of frame; the table goes silent, every head turning to follow him.
Sound: the dialogue as written, clinking cutlery and family chatter, a roar of laughter that cuts off dead, a chair scraping hard on the floor. No music.
